blocks.x: Timetable optimization quantum-inspired, path capacity up 12% on the same infrastructure and conflict resolution from hours to minutes
Identity withheld, a rail freight operator whose network was full and whose timetable had been argued into local optima over fifteen years. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter counted the contention: path requests refused despite visible slack, dispatcher conflict resolution averaging 2.3 hours per incident, and capacity studies outsourced because no internal model could trade off the constraints honestly.
The timetable was a compromise fossil: every year's patch made sense; the whole was unsolvable by hand. Slack existed but lived in the wrong places.

We rebuilt the timetable as an optimization problem worth its math: quantum-inspired decomposition handling the path-allocation formulation at network scale, constraint semantics signed off by operations and infrastructure managers alike, scenario runs reproducing seed-by-seed so planners can audit any solution, and dispatcher tooling resolving conflicts against the same model. The slack moved to where the demand is.
